title: Identify spatially variable genes by projecting to morphologically relevant curves
text: following simulated example illustrates use two main functions. First, create two-dimensional spatial coordinates:  tissue structure implicitly one-dimensional, MorphoGAM can applied extract t r coordinates.
code: set.seed(1) library(MorphoGAM) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr)  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 500) r <- 1 + 0.12 * cos(10 * theta)  xy <- cbind(   x = r * cos(theta) + rnorm(n = 500, sd = 0.05),   y = r * sin(theta) + rnorm(n = 500, sd = 0.05) )  data.frame(x=xy[,1], y=xy[,2]) |> ggplot(aes(x=x,y=y)) +   geom_point(size=0.5) + theme_bw()

title: Identify spatially variable genes by projecting to morphologically relevant curves

Alternatively, user can try several values k choose one works best. curve_fit model contains several results plots:    Note CurveFinderInteractive() opens shiny app allows user hand-draw curve.

what: Step 2: model gene expression along the curve
title: Identify spatially variable genes by projecting to morphologically relevant curves
text: MorphoGAM() takes input counts matrix n × p counts matrix Y. , generate synthetic counts matrix Y one gene variation t direction 99 variation r direction: Now can apply MorphoGAM() fit generalized additive model gene: Note design = y ~ s(t, bs = "cc") + s(r, bs="cr") fits model including smooth term t r coordinate. use bs=cc fit periodic function t direction. Common choices include: MorphoGAM provides results data frame contains gene well summaries estimated function. peak.t maximum height fitted function t log scale. range.t range fitted function t scale counts. peak.r range.r equivalent fitted function r direction. pv.t pv.r corresponding p-values null hypothesis function 0. example, wanted find gene varied t direction, sort genes largest peak.t: expected, identify gene 1, one simulated significant variation t direction. can visualize using MorphoGAM’s plotting function:  can repeat top genes r direction,
code: n_locations <- nrow(xy) n_genes <- 100  Y <- matrix(0L, nrow = n_genes, ncol = n_locations)  # Gene 1 varies along t eta_t <- log(2) - 3 * (curve_fit$xyt$t - 0.5) Y[1, ] <- rpois(n_locations, lambda = exp(eta_t))  # Genes 2–100 vary along r, with different directions and effect sizes r_effect <- rep(c(-1, 1), length.out = n_genes - 1) *   seq(1, 3, length.out = n_genes - 1)  eta_r <- log(2) +   outer(r_effect, curve_fit$xyt$r - 0.5)  Y[2:n_genes, ] <- matrix(   rpois(length(eta_r), lambda = exp(eta_r)),   nrow = n_genes - 1 )  rownames(Y) <- paste("Gene", seq_len(n_genes)) mgam <- MorphoGAM(   Y,   curve.fit = curve_fit,   design = y ~ s(t, bs = "cc") + s(r, bs="cr"),   min.count.per.gene = 10,   return.fx = TRUE ) # Variation only along the fitted curve design <- y ~ s(t, bs = "cr")  # Variation only orthogonal to the fitted curve design <- y ~ s(r, bs = "cr")  # Both directions design <- y ~ s(t, bs = "cr") + s(r, bs = "cr")  # A non-periodic smooth for a closed curve, with orthogonal variation design <- y ~ s(t, bs = "cr") + s(r, bs="cr") mgam$results |> arrange(desc(peak.t)) |> head()  ##             peak.t    range.t        pv.t     peak.r    range.r       pv.r ## Gene 1  1.49356467 5.20632298 0.000000000 0.01774403 0.04714376 0.07312087 ## Gene 38 0.06456097 0.16319422 0.001556038 0.58659871 1.62485505 0.00000000 ## Gene 24 0.03933418 0.08120660 0.018316422 0.55740478 1.28201140 0.00000000 ## Gene 80 0.03422020 0.12947207 0.003950135 0.80710312 2.68462271 0.00000000 ## Gene 97 0.02798697 0.06438621 0.009632596 1.24001522 4.81096313 0.00000000 ## Gene 91 0.02058071 0.05162055 0.015191861 1.27260655 6.30931200 0.00000000 ##         intercept ## Gene 1  -4.681794 ## Gene 38 -4.618577 ## Gene 24 -4.641936 ## Gene 80 -4.600510 ## Gene 97 -4.728496 ## Gene 91 -4.690288 MorphoGAM::plotGAMestimates(Y,  mgam_object=mgam, genes=c("Gene 1"), curve_fit=curve_fit) r_sort <- mgam$results |> arrange(desc(peak.r)) |> rownames()  MorphoGAM::plotGAMestimates(Y,  mgam_object=mgam, type="r", genes=r_sort[1:3], curve_fit=curve_fit)

title: CurveFinder: Automatically estimate curve in two-dimensional ST data — CurveFinder
text: xy numeric matrix data frame two columns representing x y coordinates data points. knn integer specifying number nearest neighbors used construct KNN graph, `"auto"` choose value 3 20 model score. Default 5. prune.outlier numeric threshold pruning outliers based distance k+1 nearest neighbor. Outliers removed distance exceeds `prune.outlier * median(nnk)`. Defaults NULL (pruning). loop logical value indicating whether curve treated loop (closed curve), `"auto"` detect loops Mapper graph. Default FALSE. knot.fx Maximum number knots used GAM smooths fitted x(t) y(t). effective value capped 10 percent number points. scale_morpho_coords logical value indicating whether scale morphologically relevant coordinates `t` `r` range [0, 1]. Default TRUE. max.comp.integer specifying maximum number disconnected components allowed KNN graph. Default 5.

title: CurveFinder: Automatically estimate curve in two-dimensional ST data — CurveFinder
text: list containing: xyt data frame x y coordinates, fitted curve parameters (`t` `r`), fitted values x y (`f1` `f2`). curve.plot ggplot object showing original data fitted curve overlaid. coordinate.plot ggplot object displaying data points color-coded fitted `t` values. residuals.plot ggplot object displaying data points color-coded fitted `r` values. model.score numeric model score used internally `knn = "auto"`. arclength approximate arclength fitted curve. span.r estimated span residual coordinate. t_v_r_span ratio fitted curve arclength residual-coordinate span.

title: MorphoGAM: Apply a GAM to morphologically relevant coordinates — MorphoGAM
text: Y numeric count matrix genes rows samples cells columns. curve.fit object produced `CurveFinder()` `CurveFinderInteractive()`, containing fitted `t` `r` coordinates sample. design formula specifying GAM design, typically including smooth terms `t` `r` `y ~ s(t) + s(r)`. Smooth terms specify `bs` use `bs = "cr"` default. shrinkage Logical; `TRUE`, shrink smooth term coefficients using `ashr`. Default `FALSE`. min.count.per.gene Minimum total count required gene fit. Genes threshold returned null/default statistics. return.fx Logical; `TRUE`, return fitted smooth terms FPCA summaries `t` `r` effects. offset Optional numeric vector model offsets. `NULL`, offsets computed logarithm column sums `Y`. knots.t Optional numeric vector specifying knot locations smooth term `t`. knots.r Optional numeric vector specifying knot locations smooth term `r`.

title: MorphoGAM: Apply a GAM to morphologically relevant coordinates — MorphoGAM
text: list containing: results data frame one row per gene columns `peak.t`, `range.t`, `pv.t`, `peak.r`, `range.r`, `pv.r`, `intercept`. dispersion numeric vector negative-binomial size estimates (theta) row order `Y`, named row names present. Skipped genes `NA`. fitted mean `mu`, `mgcv::nb()` uses variance `mu + mu^2 / theta`. quadratic overdispersion coefficient `1 / theta`. design model formula used adding default cubic regression spline bases unspecified smooth terms. `return.fx = TRUE`, list also includes: fxs.t matrix fitted smooth terms `t` (genes samples). fxs.r matrix fitted smooth terms `r` (genes samples). fpca.t `irlba` decomposition `fxs.t`, available. fpca.r `irlba` decomposition `fxs.r`, available.

title: Plot depth-normalized counts with fitted GAM overlay — plotGAMestimates
text: Columns (cells/samples) depth-normalized dividing library size (column sum) multiplying median library size across columns. type = "t", x-axis uses curve_fit$xyt$t fitted values come mgam_object$fxs.t. type = "r", x-axis uses curve_fit$xyt$r fitted values come mgam_object$fxs.r. Fitted curves constructed \(n_{med} \cdot \exp(\beta_{g0} + f_g(x))\), \(\beta_{g0}\) gene-specific intercept \(f_g(x)\) smooth contribution gene.
